prs.title: fix: terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown
prs.author: weiguangli-io
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: SSE streams are abruptly cancelled instead of completing gracefully when a StreamableHTTP session/manager shuts down, producing ASGI 'response never completed' errors. Both PRs attack this via the same mechanism: tracking active SSE stream writers in self._sse_stream_writers so they can be closed on termination, and both PR titles independently describe the identical bug ('terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown' vs 'terminate streamable HTTP sessions on manager shutdown'). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: SSE streams are abruptly cancelled instead of completing gracefully when a StreamableHTTP session/manager shuts down, producing ASGI 'response never completed' errors. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2253 is the complete fix: it adds the closing loop in terminate() (streamable_http.py) that iterates and closes every entry in self._sse_stream_writers, AND updates streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan shutdown to call terminate() on active sessions before cancelling tasks - the orchestration that actually triggers graceful shutdown. 3218's diff only registers the GET-stream writer into that same dict (self._sse_stream_writers[GET_STREAM_KEY] = ...) and pops it in its own local cleanup path; it makes no change to streamable_http.py's terminate() loop or to streamable_http_manager.py, so on its own it doesn't alter shutdown behavior - it only closes a gap that matters once 2253's closing loop exists. (2 PRs)

prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent/duplicate in-flight JSON-RPC request ids are not rejected, so a second request reusing an id in `_request_streams` overwrites the first request's routing slot and cross-wires responses. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent/duplicate in-flight JSON-RPC request ids are not rejected, so a second request reusing an id in `_request_streams` overwrites the first request's routing slot and cross-wires responses. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a 400 rejection when a request id is already in flight, but #3221 replaces the plain `str(message.id)` key from #3063 with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`). This fixes two edge cases #3063's implementation misses: (1) integer id `1` and string id "1" collapse to the same key under `str()`, so #3063 would falsely 409 a legitimate concurrent request with a different-typed but textually identical id; (2) a JSON-RPC string id of exactly "_GET_stream" would collide with the `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel under #3063's scheme, which #3221 explicitly guards against.

members.author: keurcien
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from persisted storage never get `token_expiry_time` restored, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired stored token as valid. #1784 fixes this at the source in `_initialize()` by calling `update_token_expiry()` whenever stored tokens have `expires_in` set, so the existing proactive-refresh logic works correctly on the very next check. #2875 explicitly cites this same root cause in its own comment ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid') but instead patches around it by adding a new Step 3.5 in the 401 handler that unconditionally tries the stored refresh_token before falling through to full re-authorization. members.author: keurcien
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from persisted storage never get `token_expiry_time` restored, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired stored token as valid. #1784 fixes this at the source in `_initialize()` by calling `update_token_expiry()` whenever stored tokens have `expires_in` set, so the existing proactive-refresh logic works correctly on the very next check. #2875 explicitly cites this same root cause in its own comment ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid') but instead patches around it by adding a new Step 3.5 in the 401 handler that unconditionally tries the stored refresh_token before falling through to full re-authorization.
